cai-meo-luoc-cham-trung.name: Boiled Cải Mèo Greens with Mashed Egg Dip
aliases: Y Tý boiled cải mèo with duck egg
Hmong mountain mustard greens with egg dip
cai-meo-luoc-cham-trung.serving_basis: One shared vegetable dish for a four-person family meal.
cai-meo-luoc-cham-trung.description: Young cải mèo greens are briefly boiled and served with mashed boiled duck egg seasoned with fish sauce. Their mildly bitter, tender-crisp leaves pair with the rich, savory dip. This everyday dish is documented in Y Tý, Lào Cai; Bếp Việt has adapted the quantities for four people.
cai-meo-luoc-cham-trung.finished_dish: The leaves are tender yet still crisp, while the mashed egg dip is lightly savory, rich and spoonable.
cai-meo-luoc-cham-trung.serving: Drain the greens and serve with the mashed egg and fish sauce dip. Enjoy with steamed rice and a braised or pan-fried dish.
tips: Choose young greens and rinse carefully between the crinkled leaves.
Boil only until just tender; older stems may need extra time and should not be cooked in the same batch as tender leaves.
Chicken eggs can replace duck eggs; add fish sauce gradually.
search_terms: boiled cải mèo with egg dip
cai-meo-luoc-cham-trung.image_alt: A plate of boiled green cải mèo with a small bowl of mashed duck egg and fish sauce.
cai-meo-luoc-cham-trung.time_note: About 24 minutes; boiling time varies with the age and tenderness of the greens.

ingredients.name: Young cải mèo greens
ingredients.notes: Trim wilted leaves, rinse well and drain.

ingredients.name: Duck eggs
ingredients.notes: Boil until fully set and peel.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Add gradually to the mashed eggs.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Finely chop; optional.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use a little in the vegetable cooking water.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For boiling the greens and eggs.

preparation_steps: Trim the greens, remove tough stems and damaged leaves, rinse thoroughly between the folds, and drain.
Boil the eggs until the yolks are completely set. Peel and set aside.
cooking_steps: Bring salted water to a boil. Add the greens and cook over high heat for about 2–4 minutes, depending on tenderness; check a stem before removing.
Drain the greens. Mash the duck eggs with fish sauce and chili to the desired consistency, taste, and serve as a dip.

ngong-cai-luoc-cham-trung.name: Boiled Mustard Flower Stems with Egg Dip
aliases: Boiled mustard shoots with mashed egg
Ngồng cải with boiled egg dip
ngong-cai-luoc-cham-trung.serving_basis: One shared vegetable dish for a four-person family meal.
ngong-cai-luoc-cham-trung.description: Mustard flower stems are boiled until just tender, retaining a gentle sweetness and a crisp bite, then served with mashed boiled egg. The dish name appears on a Hanoi restaurant menu; the four-person home recipe below is Bếp Việt’s adaptation and does not claim to reproduce a restaurant formula.
ngong-cai-luoc-cham-trung.finished_dish: The mustard stems are bright green, tender and crisp; the egg dip is rich with a lightly savory finish and optional chili.
ngong-cai-luoc-cham-trung.serving: Dip the stems into the mashed egg and serve warm or slightly cooled with steamed rice and other family dishes.
tips: Choose young shoots with tender stems and buds that are not overly mature.
Separate thick stems so they cook evenly; avoid keeping the pot covered after cooking.
Season the egg lightly at first because fish sauce varies in saltiness.
search_terms: boiled mustard flower stems with egg dip
ngong-cai-luoc-cham-trung.image_alt: A plate of bright green boiled mustard flower stems with a small bowl of mashed egg and fish sauce.
ngong-cai-luoc-cham-trung.time_note: About 24 minutes; boiling time depends on the thickness of the stems.

ingredients.name: Mustard flower stems (ngồng cải)
ingredients.notes: Split thicker stems, trim tough ends and rinse well.

ingredients.name: Chicken eggs
ingredients.notes: Boil until fully set and peel.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Add gradually to the mashed egg.

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.notes: Optional; adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Finely slice; optional.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use a little in the cooking water.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For boiling the eggs and greens.

preparation_steps: Rinse the shoots, remove fibrous ends, cut into serving lengths and drain.
Boil the eggs until the yolks are fully set. Peel and mash them coarsely.
cooking_steps: Bring lightly salted water to a boil. Add the stems first for about one minute, then add leaves and tips and cook for another 2–3 minutes until just tender.
Drain the greens. Mix the mashed egg with fish sauce, lime juice and chili, taste and serve as a dip.

rau-don-luoc-mam-toi-ot.name: Boiled Wild Fern Greens with Garlic-Chili Fish Sauce
aliases: Boiled rau dớn with fish sauce
Boiled mountain fern with dipping sauce
rau-don-luoc-mam-toi-ot.serving_basis: One shared vegetable dish for a four-person family meal.
rau-don-luoc-mam-toi-ot.description: Young rau dớn fronds are boiled over high heat until tender-crisp and served with a bright garlic-chili fish sauce. Rau dớn is a fern-like wild green documented in meals across Vietnam’s mountain areas; use only plants correctly identified and sold as food.
rau-don-luoc-mam-toi-ot.finished_dish: The green fronds remain crisp-tender with a mild natural astringency, paired with a gently sweet, savory garlic-chili dip.
rau-don-luoc-mam-toi-ot.serving: Drain the greens and serve warm or lightly cooled with garlic-chili fish sauce. Pair with steamed rice and tofu or a braised dish.
tips: Buy rau dớn from a trusted food source; never forage or eat wild plants that have not been positively identified.
Trim mature, tough stems and overly old curled tips.
Boil over high heat until just cooked, then drain or briefly cool to preserve color and texture.
search_terms: wild fern greens with garlic chili
rau-don-luoc-mam-toi-ot.image_alt: A plate of boiled fern-like rau dớn fronds with a bowl of garlic-chili fish sauce.
rau-don-luoc-mam-toi-ot.time_note: About 23 minutes; boiling time depends on the tenderness of the fern shoots.

ingredients.name: Prepared young rau dớn fern greens
ingredients.notes: Buy from a trusted food vendor; trim tough stems.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: For the dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Mince; adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.notes: Adjust the acidity to taste.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Dissolve into the dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use a little in the boiling water.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For boiling the greens.

preparation_steps: Rinse the greens several times, remove tough stems and drain. Use only plants sourced and identified as food.
Mince the garlic and chili. Dissolve the sugar in lime juice and a spoonful of warm water, then stir in the fish sauce.
cooking_steps: Bring lightly salted water to a boil. Add the greens and cook over high heat for about 3–5 minutes until the stems are just tender; test a piece before removing.
Drain the greens. Briefly rinse with cool water if desired to retain color and bite. Add the garlic and chili to the fish sauce, taste, and serve alongside.

rau-lui-luoc-mam-cua-gia-lai.name: Gia Lai Boiled Rau Lủi with Crab Ferment Dip
aliases: Boiled Gia Lai forest greens with crab sauce
Boiled kim thất with crab dip
rau-lui-luoc-mam-cua-gia-lai.serving_basis: One shared vegetable dish for a four-person family meal.
rau-lui-luoc-mam-cua-gia-lai.description: Gia Lai rau lủi is boiled until just tender, retaining its crisp texture and distinctive aroma, then dipped in mắm cua. This way of serving the green is documented in Central Highlands food writing. Rau lủi has alternate leaves with serrated edges and purplish stems, unlike the divided fern fronds of rau dớn.
rau-lui-luoc-mam-cua-gia-lai.finished_dish: The rau lủi is green, crisp and lightly aromatic; the crab dip is deeply savory and should be used sparingly.
rau-lui-luoc-mam-cua-gia-lai.serving: Serve warm or lightly cooled with ready-to-eat mắm cua. Enjoy with steamed rice and a mild soup; use a packaged product with clear sourcing and storage instructions.
tips: Buy rau lủi positively identified and sold as food; do not substitute unidentified wild plants.
Mắm cua is fermented: use a ready-to-eat product from a traceable source and follow its storage label; this recipe does not instruct home fermentation of raw crab.
If the dip is very thick, thin it only as directed on the product label and taste before adding seasoning.
search_terms: boiled kim thất with crab dip
rau-lui-luoc-mam-cua-gia-lai.image_alt: A plate of boiled rau lủi with alternate toothed leaves and purplish stems, served with a bowl of mắm cua.
rau-lui-luoc-mam-cua-gia-lai.time_note: About 23 minutes; boiling time depends on the tenderness of the shoots.

ingredients.name: Young rau lủi greens
ingredients.notes: Choose fresh food-grade greens with tender stems and leaves.

ingredients.name: Ready-to-eat mắm cua
ingredients.notes: Use a traceable product with clear storage instructions.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Finely slice and add to the dip if desired.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For boiling the greens.

preparation_steps: Trim wilted leaves and tough ends, rinse the greens several times under running water, and drain.
Check the label and storage guidance on the ready-to-eat mắm cua. Prepare a clean serving bowl and slice the chili if using.
cooking_steps: Bring a wide pot of water to a boil. Add the rau lủi and boil for about 3–5 minutes, until the stems are just tender but still crisp.
Drain the greens. Serve the ready-to-eat crab dip in a small bowl; thin it only according to the label if needed, add chili to taste, and serve.

dau-dua-luoc-sot-me.name: Boiled Yardlong Beans with Sesame Sauce
aliases: Yardlong beans with roasted sesame dressing
Vegan yardlong beans with sesame sauce
dau-dua-luoc-sot-me.serving_basis: One shared vegetable dish for a four-person family meal.
dau-dua-luoc-sot-me.description: Yardlong beans are cut into short pieces, boiled until green and crisp, then dressed with roasted sesame sauce, soy, vinegar and sesame oil. This light vegetable dish works in a vegetarian meal or as a family side; Bếp Việt has adapted the quantities from a recipe reference for four people.
dau-dua-luoc-sot-me.finished_dish: The beans are bright green with a gentle crunch, coated in a smooth sesame dressing balanced between savory, sweet and lightly tart.
dau-dua-luoc-sot-me.serving: Arrange the beans on a plate, drizzle with sesame sauce just before serving, and sprinkle with the remaining toasted sesame. Serve as part of a vegetarian or everyday family meal.
tips: Cut the beans into even pieces so they cook at the same rate.
Boil only until just tender; cool briefly in water if you want to preserve a brighter color.
Whisk the sesame sauce smooth and adjust its saltiness, acidity and thickness before dressing the beans.
dau-dua-luoc-sot-me.image_alt: A plate of green boiled yardlong bean pieces lightly dressed with sesame sauce and toasted sesame seeds.
dau-dua-luoc-sot-me.time_note: About 20 minutes; blanching time varies with bean thickness.

preparation_steps: Rinse the beans, cut them into 6–8 cm pieces, and mince the garlic.
Toast the sesame seeds if needed. Whisk the sesame sauce with half the seeds and the water until smooth; set aside the remaining sesame.
cooking_steps: Bring lightly salted water to a boil. Add the beans and cook for about 3–4 minutes until tender and green; drain or briefly cool in water.
Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, sugar, garlic and salt into a dressing. Arrange the beans on a plate, drizzle with sesame sauce, scatter the remaining sesame and serve promptly.
